transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Carla Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Iyer (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel, Ethan Cross, Samir Rao, Hannah Lee (AstraLogistics)

Summary: Quick renewal touchpoint + discussion of expansion needs (additional regions, reserved capacity bump for Q4, and contract term options). Agreed to run benchmarks in EU and AP, send pricing comparison for 12 vs 24 month commits, and circulate SOW for legal review.

00:00 Carla Nguyen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, happy to, uh, kick off. I think we have about 50 minutes, so we'll cover renewal timeline, capacity numbers for holiday, and the region expansion ask. Maya, Ethan, you good on time?
00:14 Maya Patel: Yep, all good. Thanks Carla. We just want to make sure the numbers and the SLAs line up before we sign on the extension.
00:20 Liam O'Connor: Quick intro from our side, I'm Liam on CSM, I'll be owning onboarding for any new regions and the rollout plan. Priya's gonna cover the technical bits for benchmarks and capacity.
00:33 Priya Iyer: Hi. I can run through options — Dedicated reserved capacity, burst lanes, and the private VPC rules if you want isolation.
00:42 Ethan Cross: Great. So high level — last year we went with a baseline reserved pool in us-west and then used hosted for burst. For next year we need dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1. The ask from Product is 30% higher baseline and a 2x burst in peak windows.
01:02 Carla Nguyen: Understood. On contract term — we can do 12 or 24 month committed credits. 24 month gives you a deeper discount and lock-in for pricing; 12 month keeps flexibility. We'll send a comparison.
01:15 Hannah Lee: From procurement side, we prefer 12 but procurement can approve a multi-year if the economics are better. Need to see SOW and cancellation terms.
01:26 Maya Patel: A technical question — when you say dedicated in eu and ap, are those fully isolated GPU pools with KV cache shared or, like, replicated? We have concerns about cold-starts for KV cache across regions.
01:40 Priya Iyer: Good question. Dedicated pools are separate; KV cache is per-region. We do have cross-region warmup tooling but it isn't global shared state. For your workload — because you have fairly predictable prefix patterns — we can pre-warm caches during off-peak windows and use our prefix caching to reduce token work.
01:58 Samir Rao: How about data residency and KMS? We need keys in EU for eu-west and for AP we need to use our HSM provider. Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS?
02:10 Priya Iyer: Yes, Private deployments and Dedicated both support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. There are a few steps for the key rotation and grants, we'll include the integration checklist in the security packet.
02:24 Ethan Cross: Cool. Also curious about failover — if eu-west capacity hits the cap, can we route to us-west in the same SLAs or is that an increased latency scenario?
02:36 Carla Nguyen: Smart routing can route across regions by policy, but note latency will go up when crossing continents. We can configure an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in us-west, or to hosted non-dedicated capacity if you prefer lower cost but less predictable latency. We can show latency profiles from our benchmark runs.
02:55 Maya Patel: We'll need concrete numbers — what's the p95 for a 4k context model in eu-west with Dedicated vs Hosted fallback?
03:05 Priya Iyer: Typical p95 on Dedicated with our optimized kernels for that family is around 180±10ms depending on sequence length; hosted fallback will be higher, more like 300–600ms in worst cases. We'll run a dedicated benchmark so you'll have exact numbers for your config.
03:25 Ethan Cross: Also want to confirm autoscale — can Dedicated scale up for sudden traffic and then back down within minutes? Our traffic is spiky during peak delivery windows.
03:36 Priya Iyer: Yes, we support configurable autoscaling policies. For very sudden spikes you can enable burst capacity; that draws from a shared pool and has a higher per-token rate. We can model cost for your 2x burst scenario.
03:52 Liam O'Connor: I can also coordinate a run during your expected peak so we measure real-world cold start and scale latencies.
04:00 Maya Patel: That would be great. For the benchmark, we want eu-west and ap-south — ap-south has slightly older hardware in our current infra so any model quantization guidance is useful.
04:13 Priya Iyer: We'll include quantization profiles and kernel selection notes. For AP we might recommend int8-quantized variants which trade a little accuracy for throughput. We'll surface eval metrics.
04:25 Carla Nguyen: On pricing, we talked earlier about committed vs on-demand. For the 24-month commit we can stretch the discounts and include a free burst credit the first quarter. For 12 months we give you standard commit discounts and flexible exit terms. We'll put numbers in the worksheet.
04:42 Hannah Lee: On SOW, can you show termination clauses and data retention policy? Our legal needs to see SOC 2 attestation and audit logs.
04:50 Carla Nguyen: Absolutely — SOC 2 report's included in the security pack; audit logs and longer retention is an add-on but we can include 13-month log retention under enterprise plan. I'll attach the security deck and the compliance docs after the call.
05:05 Samir Rao: One more infra question — we want VPC peering for private deployments. Is there an option to do a private control plane and on-prem gateway for air-gapped sync?
05:18 Priya Iyer: Yes, we support Private with customer-managed networking. On-prem gateway is available for larger enterprises; we'll need your network team for an architecture call.
05:28 Ethan Cross: Sounds good. Can we also get token-level cost breakdowns per model route? Product like to see dollars per 1k tokens by route and model.
05:38 Carla Nguyen: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route. We'll export a sample report for you based on current usage to help plan commits.
05:48 Maya Patel: For the benchmarks, we want to test two model families — one larger for higher quality and a smaller cheaper one for fallback. Can you support canary-style rollouts for the models?
06:00 Priya Iyer: Yep, rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback policies are supported. We can also run A/B tests and capture quality regression alerts tied to your evals.
06:12 Ethan Cross: Okay, timeline: Our renewal window is end of next month. We'd prefer to sign before Thanksgiving, but procurement might take longer. Any flexibility on start date?
06:24 Carla Nguyen: We can align contract start to your preferred date. Pricing is based on commit period; if sign happens after the quarter start we'll prorate. We can put a hold on capacity so you don't get bumped while procurement finalizes.
06:37 Hannah Lee: That hold is useful. Also we need sample invoices and PO terms for our procurement system.
06:44 Carla Nguyen: I'll include sample invoice templates and payment terms in the paperwork.
06:50 Maya Patel: One more technical — our team uses a mix of prompt caching and long-term KV. Are there recommended tuning knobs for continuous batching + KV cache to avoid cache thrash?
07:03 Priya Iyer: Yes, set shorter batching windows for low-latency routes and use prefix caching for deterministic prompts. We'll recommend a workload-specific config. We'll send initial suggested settings with the benchmark run.
07:20 Ethan Cross: On region expansion costs — any premium for ap-south? We expect some higher instance costs down there.
07:28 Carla Nguyen: Per-region base costs reflect cloud prices and instance availability — ap-south may be slightly higher. We'll include regional cost deltas in the worksheet so you can decide whether to keep read-only traffic in hosted fallback or provision Dedicated.
07:42 Samir Rao: For the scaling tests, what access do you need? We don't want service disruption.
07:49 Priya Iyer: We'll need temporary IAM role with limited rights and a list of test endpoints; we can run non-destructive load tests. We'll share the security checklist.
07:59 Liam O'Connor: I'll coordinate the calendar for the benchmark window — we can do a two-hour window in the early morning to avoid production heat.
08:08 Maya Patel: Sounds good.
08:12 Carla Nguyen: Alright, quick recap and next steps: 1) We'll send pricing worksheet + SOW (Carla) 2) Schedule benchmark runs in eu-west and ap-south (Priya + Liam) 3) Astra to provide utilization metrics and procurement PO process (Samir + Hannah) 4) Legal to review SOW and SOC 2 docs. Anything to add?
08:36 Ethan Cross: No, that's all. Thanks.
08:39 Hannah Lee: Thanks everyone.
08:41 Carla Nguyen: Thanks team — we'll follow up with the attachments and calendar invites.
08:46 Maya Patel: Appreciate it.

Attachments / references mentioned: pricing worksheet (link), security deck (link to SOC 2), benchmark plan (link stub).
